title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is computing the 'discrete' Teichmüller tower in genus 1 with one puncture. The previous page identified the extension ST_{1,1} of T_{1,1} by Z with an explicit group GL(2,Z)^~. That group has two presentations: (a) generators ρ̃, σ̃, τ̃' with ρ̃^3 = σ̃^2, where τ̃' is an involution inverting ρ̃ and σ̃; (b) three involutions r̃_0, r̃_1, r̃_∞. Here T_{1,1} is the full mapping class group of the once-punctured torus, orientation-reversing classes included, so it is GL(2,Z). Its orientation-preserving part SL(2,Z)^~ = ⟨ρ̃, σ̃ | ρ̃^3 = σ̃^2⟩ is the braid group B_3.

This page passes to the fundamental group. Let U_{1,1} = X_1 − {0}, the once-punctured torus with X_1 = R^2/Z^2, and Π_{1,1} = π_1(U_{1,1}, a_{1,1}).

(40) Presentation: Π_{1,1} = ⟨x, y, l_0' | [x,y] l_0' = 1⟩. So l_0' = [x,y]^{-1} is the loop around the puncture and Π_{1,1} is free on x and y, as the NB says.

Let L = ⟨l_0'⟩ be the 'loop' (inertia) subgroup. Aut_loc(Π_{1,1}) presumably means automorphisms preserving the conjugacy classes of the inertia subgroups.

(41) Claim: ST_{1,1} ≅ Norm_{Aut_loc}(L), i.e. automorphisms sending l_0' to l_0'^{±1} exactly, not merely up to conjugation. This is the standard way to rigidify the outer action (39), T_{1,1} ≅ Autext_loc(Π_{1,1}), to an actual action by choosing an inertia generator (a 'tangential' base point at the puncture).
- By Nielsen, every automorphism of F_2 sends [x,y] to a conjugate of [x,y]^{±1}.
- Composing with an inner automorphism lands in the normalizer of L.
- The ambiguity is conjugation by elements of the centralizer of [x,y] in F_2, namely ⟨[x,y]⟩ ≅ Z.
- So Norm(L) is an extension of GL(2,Z) by Z. Its orientation-preserving part, Stab([x,y]), is B_3. This matches GL(2,Z)^~.

Programme stated: lift the action GL(2,Z)^~ → Aut_loc(Π_{1,1}) explicitly on the generators. ρ̃ and σ̃ must fix l_0'; τ̃' = r̃_0, r̃_1 and r̃_∞ must send l_0' to l_0'^{-1}. Hence one must give their images of x and y.

To do so he passes to the Z^2-principal covering R^2∖Z^2 → U_{1,1}, induced from the universal cover R^2 → X_1. Next page: a base point a = (1/2, 1/2), x and y given by straight paths to a+e_0 and a+e_1, and Malgoire's 'mixed π_1' computation. That yields the exact sequence 1 → π_1(R^2∖Z^2) → Π_{1,1} → Z^2 → 1, and [x,y] is seen as the straight loop around the origin.
errors: Notational inconsistency only: Π_{1,1} (previous page) is written π_{1,1} here. Otherwise the statements are correct: Π_{1,1} is indeed free on x, y, and the normalizer of ⟨[x,y]⟩ in Aut(F_2) is a Z-extension of GL(2,Z), with orientation-preserving part B_3 = ⟨ρ, σ | ρ^3 = σ^2⟩.

Minor: whether Norm_{Aut_loc}(L) equals the normalizer in the full Aut(F_2) depends on the definition of Aut_loc. By Nielsen every automorphism of F_2 preserves the conjugacy class of [x,y]^{±1}, so Aut_loc = Aut(F_2) here and nothing is lost.

ideas.what: Presentation of π_1 of the once-punctured torus as free group on x, y, with the puncture loop l_0' = [x,y]^{-1}
Lifting the outer action T_{1,1} → Out(Π_{1,1}) to an actual action by normalizing the inertia subgroup L, giving a Z-extension ST_{1,1} ≅ Norm_{Aut}(L)
ideas.modern_name: mapping class group of the torus with one boundary component / tangential base point at the puncture; Stab_{Aut(F_2)}([x,y]) ≅ B_3
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nielsen (1917), Magnus–Karrass–Solitar; in the GT context Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the T_{1,1} level and the modular tower in general terms; this explicit normalizer formula is not known to me there

ideas.what: Requirement that ρ̃, σ̃ fix the puncture loop while the reflections r̃_0, r̃_1, r̃_∞ invert it
ideas.modern_name: orientation character of the extended mapping class group acting on boundary/inertia

ideas.what: Computing the action via the Z^2-cover R^2∖Z^2 and a 'mixed' fundamental group (Malgoire's calculus of couples (γ, ℓ))
ideas.modern_name: relative fundamental groupoid / orbifold π_1 via a lattice cover
ideas.usually_credited_to: Malgoire (as Grothendieck states); standard covering-space technique

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard setup: Nielsen-type identification of the lifted modular group GL(2,Z)^~ (∋ B_3) with the normalizer of the puncture-loop subgroup in Aut(F_2). All of it is classical and well documented in the later Grothendieck–Teichmüller literature. The only archival interest is the explicit pairing with the involution presentation r̃_0, r̃_1, r̃_∞ and the credit to Malgoire's method.
transcription_corrections: Margin note likely reads roughly 'justification de la notation l_0' au lieu de l_0 : pour le distinguer d'un élément ... de Gl(2,Z)!'. That is, the prime avoids a clash with a symbol already used in GL(2,Z)^~; 'discriminant' is doubtful.
'le sous-groupe-lacets de π_{1,1}': the insertion '-lacets' attaches to 'sous-groupe' (loop subgroup).
NB: '(NB π_{1,1} est le groupe libre sur les générateurs x et y)' — 'libre' is fairly clear in context; the editorial [?] marks can be dropped.
The group on this page is written π_{1,1} but is the Π_{1,1} defined in (38).
